items.text: First-choice striker Kai Havertz (hamstring, hurt with Germany 24 Sep) is now listed as unavailable for Leeds, with an October/November return.
Captain Martin Odegaard shook off his ankle knock, played for Norway against Wales and is expected to be available for Leeds.
Declan Rice skipped England duty for load management with no new injury and should be available.
Ezri Konsa came off early on England duty against Croatia and is awaiting assessment; a doubt for Leeds.
William Saliba (back) remains out, with December now seen as his possible comeback window.
Ben White (groin), Cristhian Mosquera (hamstring) and Piero Hincapie are back in training and expected to be available.
Summer signings Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa are bedding in as starters; ex-Leeds keeper Illan Meslier arrived on a free.
Beaten 3-0 at Brighton on 19 Sep, their first defeat of the season; sit 3 points behind leaders Man City, who have won all five.
Summer signing Harry Wilson (quad), who missed the Palace draw, is expected to be available for Arsenal.
Centre-back Joe Rodon (hamstring, hurt 30 Aug) is out until late October or early November; striker Mateo Joseph (ACL) is out until 2027.
Ilia Gruev is back from April's knee injury and played 90 minutes for Bulgaria; an option for the third midfield slot.
Noah Okafor withdrew from Switzerland duty amid issues with coach Murat Yakin and stayed at Leeds to train.
Unbeaten in five league games (2W 3D) and 5th despite a flat 0-0 with Palace; Arsenal away is billed as their toughest test yet.
Deadline-day winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya hurt an ankle with France U21 (3 Oct) and is doubtful; he is a fringe player so far.
Summer signing Christos Tzolis injured a hamstring 18 minutes into Greece v Netherlands (1 Oct); out up to three weeks, targeting Everton on 24 Oct.

epl_2026-10-10_Arsenal_Leeds.summary: Arsenal (2nd) return from the break after a 3-0 loss at Brighton with attacking problems: striker Kai Havertz (hamstring) is now expected to miss out and summer signing Christos Tzolis tore a hamstring with Greece, while Konsa is being assessed. Odegaard, Rice, White and Mosquera should be available. Leeds (5th, unbeaten in five) expect Harry Wilson back but still lack Joe Rodon.

items.text: Starting left-back Ian Maatsen is out 6-8 weeks with ankle tendon damage from the Forest loss (12 Sep); summer signing Matteo Ruggeri deputised.
Pau Torres (hamstring strain v Forest) missed the Spurs win but may return after the break; listed with a 10 Oct return date.
Free signing Leon Goretzka (knee) has yet to debut and is still building fitness; 10 Oct is his listed return date.
Amadou Onana (ACL) is out long-term; Marco Bizot, Brian Madjo and Alysson are also working back from knocks.
Summer rebuild: Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Emi Martinez left; ten arrivals include Nicolas Jackson and Johan Manzambi.
Unai Emery faced scrutiny after a winless four-game start (reports of internal talks if results kept sliding); eased by the 3-2 win at Spurs.
Captain Nathan Collins (calf strain, missed the last two games) could be available again at Villa Park.
Defender Sepp van den Berg, yet to play this season, and midfielder Mathias Jensen could also return after the break.
Winger Dango Ouattara, a bench option lately, is rated 25% with a virus after missing Burkina Faso's games.
Unbeaten in seven in all competitions; the 3-0 win over Chelsea on 18 Sep was called their best performance of the season.
Kevin Schade (3 league goals) is in his best form under Andrews with contract talks ongoing; Igor Thiago was left out by Brazil but is backed by his coach.
Playmaker Mikkel Damsgaard rolled an ankle for Denmark v Portugal; coach Riemer said it 'turned out to be a bigger injury'. Back at Brentford, rated 25%.

epl_2026-10-10_AstonVilla_Brentford.summary: Aston Villa (16th) finally won, 3-2 at Spurs, but are still without left-back Ian Maatsen, with Pau Torres and yet-to-debut Leon Goretzka pushing to return. Unbeaten Brentford (4th) may get captain Nathan Collins, Sepp van den Berg and Mathias Jensen back, but chief creator Mikkel Damsgaard rolled an ankle with Denmark and his coach called it 'a bigger injury', leaving him a major doubt.

items.text: Top scorer Joao Pedro (3G, 3A; knee, hurt v Hull) is unlikely to be available before late October; he also missed the Brentford loss.
Moises Caicedo (calf; just 14 minutes all season) should be fit to face Bournemouth.
Cole Palmer (minor muscle problem, pulled out of England duty) has resumed training and is expected to be available.
Reece James (hamstring, missed the Brentford loss) has resumed training and is expected to be available.
Summer signing Marco Palestra is back in training and Emmanuel Emegha is nearing a return; neither has debuted yet.
Winger Jamie Gittens (ankle, seen on crutches) is likely out; back-up keeper Mike Penders (quad) has been back on a bench.
Xabi Alonso's side are winless in three after the 3-0 loss at Brentford and have gone 22 league games without a clean sheet.
Justin Kluivert, who had started every league game, was injured at Real Sociedad (17 Sep), missed Liverpool and is out for 'some weeks'.
Eli Junior Kroupi (ankle) and Julian Araujo (thigh) are out until November; Amine Adli and Veljko Milosavljevic are not due back until about 18 Oct.
David Brooks withdrew from the Wales squad through injury on 30 Sep; he was among the substitutes against Liverpool.
New boss Marco Rose is still without a league win (0W 3D 2L) after losing 1-0 to Liverpool; he says he is confident the points will come.
Won their first-ever major European game, 2-1 at Real Sociedad on 17 Sep; Rose: 'That's Bournemouth football.'
Summer centre-back signing Antonio Silva has settled fast; Rose says he looks like he has played in the Premier League for years.
Midfielder Alex Scott injured a quad starting for England v Croatia and is expected to miss a couple of months, back around December.

epl_2026-10-10_Chelsea_Bournemouth.summary: Xabi Alonso's Chelsea (10th, winless in three) get bodies back: Palmer, Reece James and Palestra are training and Caicedo should be fit, but top scorer Joao Pedro (knee) is now unlikely before late October. Marco Rose's Bournemouth (17th, still winless) lose midfielder Alex Scott until around December after a quad injury on his first England start, on top of Kluivert, Kroupi, Adli and Araujo.

items.text: Suspended: winger Abdul Fatawu serves a one-match ban after a second yellow for simulation in the 1-0 defeat at Everton (19 Sep).
Midfielder Jack Taylor (knee) remains sidelined; Jaden Philogene is expected to make his first league start of the season in place of Fatawu.
New manager Gary O'Neil has two wins from five, incl. a 3-2 win at Palace, already half the club's win total from their last top-flight season.
Left-back Leif Davis is in form, with two goals and an assist in three league games before the Everton trip.
Alvaro Arbeloa, appointed after Marco Silva left for Benfica, is under pressure; Football Insider says Fulham have sounded out Thomas Frank.
Winless in five (0W 2D 3L) and 19th, but drew with Liverpool (0-0) and Man United (1-1); run v the three promoted sides seen as season-defining.
Captain Tom Cairney (knee, due back about 17 Oct) and right-back Kenny Tete (concussion) remain out; Castagne and Robinson are the full-backs.
Creative winger Harry Wilson left for Leeds on a free transfer in the summer.

epl_2026-10-10_Ipswich_Fulham.summary: Promoted Ipswich (11th) have two wins under Gary O'Neil but are without winger Abdul Fatawu, suspended after two yellows at Everton; Jaden Philogene is expected to make his first league start in his place. Fulham (winless in five, 2 points) keep Alvaro Arbeloa under pressure, with reports the club has sounded out Thomas Frank. Tom Cairney and Kenny Tete remain out for Fulham.

items.text: Benjamin Sesko (long-standing shin problem) missed the Fulham draw and Slovenia duty; still no return date and he faces a fitness test.
Patrick Dorgu hurt his hamstring after 30 minutes for Denmark and was sent home; no return date, rated a major doubt for Spurs.
Noussair Mazraoui (back, hurt with Morocco) still needs assessing, which leaves United thin at full-back.
Bruno Fernandes played for Portugal later in the break after missing the Norway game; expected to be fit barring a late problem.
Rashford and Mainoo, who both pulled out of England duty, are likely to be available for selection.
Amad Diallo (ankle, out all season) is hoped to make the bench; summer signing Carlos Baleba is ready for his debut after an ankle injury.
De Ligt (back) is closing in on a return but has no date; Ugarte (knee surgery) is out; keepers Darlow and Heaton are both doubts.
Pressure is mounting on Michael Carrick: one league win in five, three defeats in seven games in all competitions, and a late equaliser needed at Fulham.
Summer signings Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Darlow are already in the recent results; Hojlund, Casemiro and Sancho left.
Pedro Porro (hamstring) is out until about 19 October. He is the only senior right-back, so Archie Gray is likely to deputise.
Centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke left the Netherlands camp with a foot problem; reports call it minor but his return date is unknown.
Micky van de Ven hurt a finger when Jovic landed on his arm for the Netherlands; not serious and he is expected to play.
Dejan Kulusevski is training after 16 months out but is being managed day by day; a return is pencilled in for October or November.
Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert (both ACL) and Mykhailo Mudryk (ankle, due back about 31 October) are still out.
Kudus, back from an eight-month quad injury with four sub appearances, was released by Ghana to keep recovering at Spurs.
De Zerbi is the bookmakers' favourite for the next Premier League sacking after £300m+ of spending; Pochettino is being mentioned.
Bottom of the table with two goals in five league games, despite averaging 60.6% possession (third-highest in the league).
Summer signings Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Savio and Marmoush are already in the recent results, but the much-changed side has yet to click.

epl_2026-10-10_ManUnited_Tottenham.summary: Both managers are under pressure: Carrick's United have one league win in five, and De Zerbi's Spurs are bottom and winless with two goals in five. United came out of the break with Sesko, Dorgu and Mazraoui doubtful, but Bruno, Rashford and Mainoo should play and Amad and Baleba are close. Spurs are without Porro; Van de Ven should be fine but Van Hecke is a doubt.

items.text: Ever-present centre-back Dan Ballard (hamstring, hurt with Northern Ireland 25 Sep) is expected to miss Brighton; reports fear months out.
Striker Brian Brobbey (suspected hamstring, hurt with the Netherlands 24 Sep) is a major doubt, rated 25%; severity not confirmed.
Key midfielder Noah Sadiki, who limped off for DR Congo on 28 Sep, is rated a 50% doubt with a knock.
Left-back Reinildo is back from his one-match ban; Le Bris must choose between him and Dayann Methalie.
Habib Diarra (hamstring) had a scan and Brighton may come too soon; Romaine Mundle (knee) is out until around January.
One win in five (1W 1D 3L) and 14th; conceded five in a 5-3 defeat at Man City just before the break.
Striker Babis Kostoulas (4 goals, 3 assists in 8 games) needed stitches after a leg knock on Greece duty but is recovering well.
Mats Wieffer (knee), Jack Hinshelwood and Femi Azeez are targeting returns this weekend; Yankuba Minteh (calf) stays out until late October.
Captain Lewis Dunk (neck) is expected to return; Pascal Struijk (hamstring) and Yasin Ayari (cold) are rated 50% doubts.
Kaoru Mitoma (hamstring) is nearing a first appearance of the season; Evan Ferguson (ankle) and Stefanos Tzimas (knee) remain out.
Summer midfield signing Chema Andres has impressed and headed in the third goal in the 3-0 win over Arsenal.
3rd with the league's best goal difference (+11) after winning 5-0 at Coventry and beating Arsenal 3-0 in their last two league games.

epl_2026-10-10_Sunderland_Brighton.summary: Brighton (3rd, best goal difference) are flying after 5-0 at Coventry and 3-0 over Arsenal, with Dunk expected back and Mitoma, Wieffer and Hinshelwood nearing returns, though Minteh stays out. Sunderland (14th) are braced to be without ever-present centre-back Dan Ballard (hamstring), striker Brian Brobbey is a major doubt and Habib Diarra looks unlikely; Reinildo is back from his ban.

items.text: QB Michael Penix Jr. (partial ACL tear) starts again after his Week 3 return (18/25, 256 yds vs GB); Cooper Rush started Weeks 1-2, both losses.
CB1 A.J. Terrell Jr. (groin) on IR since Sep 22 and missed Week 3; C.J. Henderson starts, CB Robert Longerbeam signed.
Tua Tagovailoa is Penix's backup tonight; Cooper Rush is the inactive emergency third QB.
RB Bijan Robinson named NFC Offensive Player of the Week (194 rush yds, 2 TD vs GB; 467 scrimmage yds in 3 games).
RB Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) placed on IR, out at least four games; Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller share the load
Inactive: LB Kaden Elliss (calf), DE Carl Granderson (ankle), edge Anfernee Jennings (knee). LB Pete Werner (shoulder) is active.
LT Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) went on IR Sep 23 and missed Week 3; remains out.
Blew a 27-16 third-quarter lead vs Las Vegas with four fourth-quarter turnovers; Moore wants team to 'keep going' after emotional loss.
QB Tyler Shough confirmed starter; threw career-high 4 TDs vs Raiders but has been sacked on 20% of pressures.
DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring, missed Week 3) and green-dot LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) are active; LB Yasir Abdullah (illness) also dressed.
Signed WR Kevin Austin Jr. to the active roster; RB Ulysses Bentley IV and edge David Ojabo added to the practice squad
TE Noah Fant (abdomen) and rookie DT Christen Miller are inactive; Juwan Johnson handles tight end.
Falcons inactives are all depth: QBs Rush (emergency 3rd) and Strand, DBs Dewalt and Longerbeam, DE Jared Ivey, OL Ethan Onianwa.

Inactives are in: New Orleans is without LB Kaden Elliss, edges Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings and TE Noah Fant, but LB Pete Werner plays; RB Travis Etienne Jr. is on IR. Atlanta has every starter available, with Samson Ebukam and Divine Deablo both cleared, a week after routing Green Bay in Michael Penix Jr.'s return.

LT Jake Matthews (groin), DE Samson Ebukam and LB Divine Deablo, all listed as questionable, are active.

Trey Hendrickson, new center Cam Jurgens and guard Andrew Vorhees are also inactive, but Zay Flowers and Marlon Humphrey are active. Atlanta (2-2) sits edge Za'Darius Smith, while left tackle Jake Matthews is active and Michael Penix Jr. has the offense rolling.

items.text: Bills lost 29-26 at home to New England in Week 4; WR Keon Coleman (ankle) and edge Bradley Chubb (thumb) practiced fully Friday.
Edge Myles Garrett (knee) has been on injured reserve since Sept. 13 and will not play.
TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is on injured reserve.
DL Ed Oliver (knee) and WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder, hurt in Friday's practice) are ruled out.
WR D.J. Moore (shoulder), CB Dee Alford (ankle) and DL Landon Jackson (knee) are questionable; all travel and will be decided by game time.
CB Christian Benford (toe), who missed Week 4, is good to go and expected to start, with Maxwell Hairston opposite; WR Skyler Bell makes his debut.
DE Aaron Donald (back), TE Colby Parkinson and CB Jaylen Watson carry no game status; Donald and Parkinson each missed only Week 4.
S Quentin Lake (hip) is questionable but trending in the right direction, Sean McVay said; LBs Stewart, Stuard and Landman have no status.

items.text: DTs Mason Graham (knee/ankle), Mike Hall Jr. (ankle) and Kalia Davis (quad) are all out, leaving Cleveland without three interior linemen.
